monthly_review.summary: This month shows a deliberate shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic development — evidenced by increased Z1/Z2 time and reduced HR — though at the cost of some speed maintenance and training effect depth.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 increased from 55% to 83% this month, while Z4+Z5 dropped from 19% to 1%, indicating a strong intentional focus on foundational aerobic work.

goal_tracker.message: You need 3.7 more km across 2 remaining sessions (e.g., two 2.0 km easy runs) to match last month’s volume — achievable with minimal strain given your current aerobic emphasis.

insights.title: Efficiency dip aligns with slower pace & lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.66 to 13.37 this month, coinciding with avg pace slowing by +28 sec/km and avg HR dropping 7 bpm — suggesting recent runs prioritized recovery over neuromuscular coordination or metabolic stimulus.

insights.title: Near-total absence of threshold and VO2 max work
insights.body: Z4 (1%) and Z5 (0%) represent just 0.3 km of total May volume — down from 19% (7.2 km) in April — meaning no meaningful lactate threshold or VO2 max stimulus this month despite stable VO2 max (37.0).

insights.title: Cadence improved but stride length variability increased
insights.body: Cadence rose from 142 to 145 spm, yet stride length swung from 66.5 cm (May 6) to 94.4 cm (May 16), correlating with the only sub-8:00 min/km effort (7:45) — suggesting form becomes less economical under faster efforts without consistent Z3+ practice.

insights.title: Strong recovery signals in recent long run
insights.body: The May 6 long run (9.5 km @ 131 bpm, 141 spm, 351 ms ground contact) shows low HR and moderate efficiency (13.37) — consistent with well-managed fatigue and effective aerobic base work.

recommendations.action: Do one 4.0 km Zone 3 run (HR 145–155 bpm) at ~435–450 sec/km (7:15–7:30 min/km) before May ends — e.g., May 25.
recommendations.reason: To reintroduce threshold stimulus missing this month (Z3 was only 15% vs 26% last month) and support VO2 max maintenance (currently stable at 37.0 but unsupported by recent Z4/Z5 work).

recommendations.action: Add 30 seconds of cadence-focused strides (160+ spm) after your next 2 easy runs — keeping stride length ≤72 cm per Garmin feedback.
recommendations.reason: Cadence improved (+3 spm) but stride length inconsistency (66.5–94.4 cm) suggests neuromuscular control needs reinforcement; strides will promote rhythm without elevating HR.

recommendations.action: Perform one 6.0 km Zone 2 run (HR 125–135 bpm) at 540–570 sec/km (9:00–9:30 min/km) with ground contact time <320 ms (use real-time Garmin metric if available).
recommendations.reason: Your best recent GC time is 286 ms (May 16), but average is 314 ms — lowering GC improves efficiency and matches your rising cadence trend.

weekly_focus.description: Balance foundational endurance (Z2) with brief, controlled intensity (Z3) and form-aware drills to stabilize efficiency gains while preventing neuromuscular deconditioning.
suggested_sessions: 6.0 km Zone 2 run (HR 125–135 bpm, GC <320 ms)
4.0 km Zone 3 run (HR 145–155 bpm, pace ~440 sec/km)
